## Research Memo — Cycle of 2026-08-27

### Market Read
Broad tape is constructive: record U.S. corporate profits (+22.8% YoY in Q2) and record foreign inflows into U.S. equities are supportive tailwinds for the SPY/QQQ core. Two structural sector stories stand out today: (1) bank regulators continuing a multi-year pivot toward lighter-touch, financial-risk-only supervision — a tailwind for bank multiples — and (2) Google's antitrust overhang has been meaningfully de-risked now that the court rejected structural remedies. Meanwhile Meta just cleared a major legal cloud (teen-safety settlement) and Nvidia is dealing with a self-inflicted governance headline (paused AI-cloud revenue-share deals) that doesn't change my thesis since I hold no NVDA.

### Book Shape Problem (address first)
The account is currently **5 positions, not the target ~12**, and two names breach the 22% hard cap: **AMZN (25.6% of budget)** and **GOOGL (27.1%)**. This concentration is the single biggest risk in the book right now — not any one thesis being broken. I'm trimming both back toward ~20% to (a) restore compliance and (b) fund diversification into sectors the book currently lacks entirely (healthcare, financials).

### Judging existing holdings against a stated thesis/target/stop

- **GOOGL** — Thesis: Search+Cloud growth at a discount multiple; antitrust risk was the main overhang. That risk has now been reduced — the court rejected Chrome/Android divestiture and imposed only behavioral remedies, and 
total quarterly revenue reached $113.83 billion, with Google Search delivering 17% year-over-year growth and Google Cloud continuing its surge as an AI infrastructure provider
, with 
the market has largely shrugged off antitrust concerns
. Thesis intact, value-scan confirms it's still cheap. Target $400 / Stop $290. Action: **trim to ~20% weight** (cap compliance), not a sell of the thesis.

- **AMZN** — No prior thesis; stating one now: AWS reacceleration + ad growth + retail margin expansion. Not flagged rich or cheap by the scan — a fair-value core holding, oversized only due to cap breach. Target $300 / Stop $220. Action: **trim to ~20% weight**.

- **META** — Thesis: AI-driven ad monetization + capex payoff. This just got stronger: Rosenblatt 
raised its price target on Meta to $886 from $883 and maintained a 'Buy' rating
 after the teen-safety settlement, which analysts called 
"less punitive than feared"
. Thesis intact and improving. Target $700 / Stop $480. Action: **hold, no add** — book is already tech-heavy (4 of 5 names); don't compound the concentration.

- **MSFT** — Thesis: Azure/Copilot enterprise AI adoption. Small (12.2%), up 2%, thesis intact, no news breaking it. Target $580 / Stop $440. **Hold.**

- **SPY** — Thesis: core beta exposure to a market benefiting from record profit growth and record foreign buying. Small (9%), thesis intact. Target: trim if SPY re-rates sharply above trend; Stop $650 on a real drawdown. **Hold.**

None of these are stop-loss situations — all P&L moves are sub-1% noise, not thesis breaks.

### New positions (diversification into underrepresented sectors)

- **UNH — BUY ~$70 (medium conviction).** Value scan flags it undervalued after last year's guidance-cut shock. Confirmed by fundamentals: Q2 2026 
delivered a powerhouse performance... driven by a massive, surprise improvement in its core medical underwriting margins
 with the 
Medical Care Ratio to 86.7%
 and EPS guidance raised sharply. Morningstar lifted fair value to $475 but also cautions 
shares look fairly valued after rising over 30% since the beginning of the year
 — so I'm sizing medium, not full, given the re-rate has already partly closed the gap. Target $460 / Stop $340. Adds healthcare exposure the book completely lacks.

- **JPM — BUY ~$55 (starter/medium conviction).** No single-name value-scan flag, but the sector tailwind is real: regulators are 
focus on material financial risks and less so on soft risks such as reputational risks
, easing the supervisory burden and supporting bank multiples/capital-return capacity industry-wide. Adds financials exposure — a sector completely absent from the book. Target $400 / Stop $310.

### What I'm NOT doing
- **NVDA**: Watchlist name, no value-scan edge either way. The WSJ report that 
Nvidia has paused some deals in a new financing initiative that offered credit support to AI cloud companies in exchange for a share of revenue
 is a governance/antitrust-optics story, not a demand problem — but with no fundamental mispricing flagged, chasing it here would violate the "don't buy what's already priced in" rule.
- **AAPL, TSLA, WMT, COST**: All explicitly flagged rich by the value scan — avoid.

### Trades this cycle
| Action | Ticker | ~$ Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SELL | AMZN | ~$56 (trim to $200/20%) | Cap compliance, thesis intact |
| SELL | GOOGL | ~$71 (trim to $200/20%) | Cap compliance, thesis intact & undervalued |
| BUY | UNH | ~$70 | Medium conviction, healthcare diversifier, Target $460 / Stop $340 |
| BUY | JPM | ~$55 | Starter/medium, financials diversifier, Target $400 / Stop $310 |

Net effect: book moves from 5 to 7 positions, two cap breaches resolved, two new sectors (healthcare, financials) added, ~$100 cash retained for next cycle's diversification (V, JNJ, or XLE candidates) rather than forcing all 12 slots in one costly turn. **Recommendation: execute the two trims and two starter buys above; otherwise hold everything else — no reason to touch MSFT, META, or SPY this cycle.**

audit.summary: This was a clean, well-reasoned cycle. The manager correctly identified the real problem (AMZN/GOOGL breaching the 22% hard cap) and addressed it directly with modest trims rather than full exits, explicitly noting the theses on both remain intact - that's honest, not a black-box move. The UNH buy is well-supported: it matches the value scan's undervalued flag, cites specific medical-cost-ratio improvement and raised guidance, and is sized down (medium conviction) specifically because the manager acknowledges Morningstar's caution that shares have already re-rated - that kind of self-skepticism is exactly what I want to see. Stated targets/stops are given for every position, including previously thesis-less holdings (AMZN, META, MSFT, SPY), which is good hygiene going forward. One minor gap: the JPM buy is mentioned in the memo and trade table but doesn't appear in the actual order list, so I'm only auditing the three orders given - no issue there. Diversification progress (adding healthcare) is genuine and consistent with the stated book-shape problem, not a random chase. Nothing here contradicts the memo's own risk flags, and no rich-valuation names (AAPL/TSLA/WMT/COST) or hype-only trades (NVDA) were bought despite favorable headlines - good discipline. All three orders approved.
